title: The Lost City of Z (part 2)
text: The interior of Brazil was so forbidding, however, that some tribes managed to insulate themselves, for a time, from the age of airplanes and telephones. The Brazilian government didn't officially approach many Amazon tribes until the nineteen-forties, and there are still some forty tribes that have had no recorded contact with outsiders. In recent decades, the Brazilian government has stopped trying to "modernize" indigenous peoples, and has worked to protect them. As a result, many Amazon tribes, particularly those in the Mato Grosso ("Thick Forest") region, where Fawcett disappeared, have flourished. Their populations, after being decimated, are growing again; their languages and customs have endured.
